\begin{quote}
Consider any two-player game of the following form (where letters indicate arbitrary payoffs):

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Player 1 ~Player 2 & \(b_1\) & \(b_2\) \\

\(a_1\) & \(u, v\) & \(\ell, m\) \\
\(a_2\) & \(w, x\) & \(y, z\) \\
\end{longtable}
}

Show that a mixed strategy Nash equilibrium always exists in this game. {[}\emph{Hint:} Define player 1's strategy to be his probability of choosing action \(a_1\) and player 2's to be his probability of choosing \(b_1\); then examine the best-response correspondences of the two players.{]}
